subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw make memory trust/provenance a native memory contract across default backends, or leave trust-scored memories to external MCP/plugin packages for now?
rationale: The request touches security posture, memory schema/API design, config surface, plugin SDK compatibility, and user-visible retrieval policy; automation can prove the gap, but maintainers must choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Design native trust metadata
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical trust-tagging thread for framework-assigned source trust, persisted memory metadata, retrieval-time policy, and migration/SDK changes.

options.title: Defer to external plugins
options.body: Close or split this only if maintainers decide current plugin/MCP seams are sufficient and OpenClaw should not own default memory trust enforcement.

options.title: Split into provenance MVP first
options.body: Use a smaller provenance/schema issue as prerequisite work, then keep trust scoring, review gates, and expiration as explicit follow-up policy work.

recommendation.title: Design native trust metadata
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical trust-tagging thread for framework-assigned source trust, persisted memory metadata, retrieval-time policy, and migration/SDK changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest available routing signal for the memory host SDK and memory-core contract boundary, and he has prior review context on this issue.
